starlight-blue.note: The only domain-independent accent, and the only tone deliberately identical in both themes.

ember-amber-night.note: Tasks, dark surface. Hand re-stepped, not derived.

verdant-signal.note: Habits, light surface. Muted on purpose — a logged habit reads as nominal, not as a reward.

sodium-gold.note: Finance, light surface. Re-stepped 2026-09-01 from #faeb20, which sat at oklch(92.3% 0.191) and 1.18:1 on Paper Field. Now 3.75:1, inside the Sibling Band between tasks (3.14) and habits (3.90). Named for the sodium-vapour lamp, which is this amber-gold rather than a spectral yellow.

sodium-gold-night.note: Finance, dark surface. Re-stepped 2026-09-01 from #faeb20, which read 14.61:1 on Deep Field and was by far the loudest tone on a dark screen. Now 7.35:1, matching tasks (7.18). Same lightness step as its light counterpart's siblings, hand-authored rather than derived.

oxblood-seal.note: Passwords, light surface. Doubles as the system destructive tone.

instrument-panel.note: Night cards, sidebar, headers. One tonal step above the field — this step IS the elevation.

hairline-grey.note: Night borders, dividers, scrollbar thumbs, unlit streak pips.

readout-white.note: Night primary text. Off-white, never pure white — pure white glares on a near-black field.

dim-label.note: Night secondary text, inactive nav, hints, units.

paper-field.note: Day page background. Warm, not clinical.

plot-1.note: Categorical chart slot 1. Fixed order — the set was validated together for CVD and contrast on both surfaces. Night value #3987e5.

plot-6.note: Categorical chart slot 6. Identical in both themes.

plot-income.note: Signed positive values only. Night value #199e70.

plot-expense.note: Signed negative values only. Night value #e66767.

display.purpose: The 48px timer readout. One per screen, and only where a number is the entire point.

headline.purpose: Page titles — every surface's H1 at 24px. Auth screens drop to 20px, the wordmark to 18px. Deliberately never bold.

title.purpose: Card, dialog and empty-state titles at 16px/500, via the font-heading utility.

body.purpose: Everything the user reads, plus nav items, section headings and list rows. 14px carries most of the hierarchy.

readout.purpose: Stat values, currency and counts. Mono marks a number as a measurement; always tinted with the owning domain tone.

label.purpose: Hints, units, timestamps, secondary lines. Rendered in the dim neutral.

eyebrow.purpose: The uppercase phase label above the timer. The only uppercase text in the system.

shadows.name: flat
shadows.purpose: The default. Surfaces separate with ring-1 ring-foreground/10 plus one tonal step — the ring IS the elevation.

shadows.name: overlay
shadows.purpose: Radix popover and select content only — elements that genuinely leave the plane. Paired with the same hairline ring.

shadows.name: tooltip
shadows.purpose: Chart tooltips, where the surface must read clearly over dense plotted ink.

shadows.name: translucency
shadows.purpose: Sidebar and floating panels over a 70%-opacity surface. Reads as translucency, not lift.

motion.name: state
motion.purpose: The default. 22 of the app's transitions are transition-colors — state changes recolor, they don't move.

motion.name: atmosphere
motion.purpose: Spotlight gradient fade and the timer progress arc — the slow layer.

motion.name: breathe
motion.value: @keyframes breathe { 0%,100% { transform: scale(1) } 50% { transform: scale(1.015) } } 4s ease-in-out infinite
motion.purpose: The running Pomodoro assembly. A breath, not a pulse. Gated behind motion-safe:.

motion.name: marquee
motion.value: @keyframes marquee { from { transform: translateX(0) } to { transform: translateX(-50%) } } linear infinite
motion.purpose: Overflowing text at a constant 40px/second — duration computed from measured width so all marquees move at the same speed.

motion.name: press
motion.purpose: Button active state. One pixel of travel, suppressed on menu triggers.

motion.name: reduced-motion
motion.purpose: Global kill switch. Every animation in the app collapses; no per-component opt-in needed.

narrative.overview:
Noctis is a dim room built so the readings glow. Every surface decision serves one purpose: lower the luminance and the chatter of the chrome so that the things the user actually came to read — a timer counting down, a seven-day streak, a month's cashflow, a balance — are the brightest things on the screen. The interface dims itself so the instruments stay legible. That is the whole thesis, and it is why the product is called Noctis.

The room is genuinely dark. Dark mode is not a theme applied over a light design; the two modes are separately authored, and the accent tones are re-stepped per surface rather than inverted. Depth is achieved the way it is in an actual instrument panel: hairline seams and tonal shifts between adjacent surfaces, not shadows floating things off the plane. The one exception is the one place it should be — genuine overlays that really do sit above everything else.

Density is deliberate and tight. Controls are 32px tall, cards step in 16px, labels run 12px. This is a single-user instrument operated by someone who already knows where everything is, so the space goes into separating readings from one another, not into making the interface feel spacious. Color is the navigation system: each domain owns one hue, and that hue appears as a 4px rail, a 14%-mix chip, and an icon tint — never as a wash across a whole surface.
keyCharacteristics: Dark-first, with both themes separately authored and independently contrast-checked
Flat surfaces separated by hairline rings; shadows reserved for true overlays
One hue per domain, used as a signal at small scale, never as a background wash
Monospace is for numbers only — it marks a value as a reading
Compact and precise: 32px controls, 16px card rhythm, 12px labels
Charts are the brightest ink on the page; chrome recedes beneath them

rules.name: The Signal Rule
rules.body: A domain tone never becomes a background. It appears as a 4px rail, a color-mix(… 14%, transparent) chip behind an icon or an active nav item, a 2px section dot, a 1.5×4px streak pip, or an icon tint. If a domain tone is filling more than roughly a tenth of a surface, the surface is wrong, not the tone.

rules.name: The Fixed Order Rule
rules.body: Chart series take plot-1 through plot-6 in declaration order. The order is fixed because it was validated as a set for color-vision deficiency and for contrast on both surfaces. Reordering to "look better" silently breaks that validation.

rules.name: The Separate Authorship Rule
rules.body: Every token that changes between themes is written by hand for its surface. No token is derived from its counterpart by inversion, lightening, or an automatic filter. A new color needs two values, checked independently.

rules.name: The Sibling Band Rule
rules.body: All four domain tones occupy one bounded band, and a fifth would have to join it. On the light surface: lightness 46–65%, chroma 0.095–0.130, landing between 3.1:1 and 7.2:1 against Paper Field. On the dark surface: lightness 57–72%, chroma 0.100–0.125, landing between 3.9:1 and 7.4:1 against Deep Field. A tone outside that band does not read as a sibling — it reads as an alarm. Measure before adding one.

rules.name: The Numerals Rule
rules.body: If it is a number the user reads as a measurement — a duration, a count, a streak, an amount — it is JetBrains Mono. If it is a number inside a sentence, it is not. Mono is a semantic marker here, not a style.

rules.name: The Weight-Not-Size Rule
rules.body: Below the page title, hierarchy is carried by weight (400 → 500) and color (Dim Label → Readout White), not by type scale. Body, nav, and section headings all sit at 14px. Only three things earn a larger size: the page title (24px), a card title (16px), and a genuine readout.

rules.name: The Three Jobs Rule
rules.body: Geist names, Plex explains, JetBrains measures. A family is never chosen for texture — if a face is being used for a fourth reason, the reason is wrong.

rules.name: The One Scroller Rule
rules.body: The shell owns the viewport; only <main> scrolls. Anything that would make the document itself scroll is a bug, not a layout choice.

rules.name: The Five Rule
rules.body: The mobile bottom nav carries five destinations. When an eighth domain arrives, it goes to the top bar and the command palette — not into the bar.

rules.name: The Off-Plane Rule
rules.body: A shadow means the element has physically left the page. If it is still part of the layout, it gets a hairline ring and a tonal step instead.

rules.name: The Round-Means-Status Rule
rules.body: A fully rounded shape signals state, not action. Pills, pips, and dots report; rectangles with 10px corners are the things you click.

dos: Do author both theme values by hand for any new color, check each against its own surface, and confirm it lands inside the Sibling Band before shipping it.
Do reach for a family by its variable — --font-display/--font-heading for Geist, --font-body for Plex, --font-mono for JetBrains. Never by class name.
Do use JetBrains Mono for any number the user reads as a measurement, tinted with the owning domain tone.
Do carry a domain tone at signal scale — a 4px rail, a 14% mix chip, a 2px dot, an icon tint — and let the surface underneath stay neutral.
Do separate surfaces with ring-1 ring-foreground/10 and one tonal step.
Do keep controls at 32px and card rhythm at 16px. Density is the point.
Do gate every animation behind motion-safe:; the global reduced-motion block handles the rest.
Do assign chart series plot-1 through plot-6 in fixed order.
Do size mobile inputs at 16px and drop to 14px at md, so iOS doesn't zoom.
donts: Don't add a shadow to something that is still part of the layout. Shadows mean the element genuinely floats.
Don't introduce a domain tone outside the Sibling Band. High chroma reads as an alarm, not as a category — that is why Finance is gold and not spectral yellow.
Don't fill a card, header, or panel background with a domain tone. The Signal Rule caps it at roughly a tenth of a surface.
Don't create hierarchy by enlarging type below the display readout. Change weight and color; body, nav, and section headings share 14px.
Don't put pure white text on Deep Field. Readout White (#e8e9ed) exists because pure white glares on a near-black field.
Don't let the document scroll. Only <main> scrolls; the shell is exactly one viewport.
Don't add a sixth item to the mobile bottom nav.
Don't drift toward enterprise density — no 11px grey-on-grey tables, no nested nav levels, no columns the user didn't ask for. Compact is not a terminal.
Don't drift toward consumer-cute — no mascot illustrations, no pastel blob backgrounds, no emoji-led empty states. The Empty component states the fact and offers the action.
Don't use a heavy or colored border for emphasis. Emphasis is a 14% tone chip or a 4px rail.
